definition.simple: The basic building block of all living things. Just like a house is made of bricks, your body is made of billions of tiny cells.
definition.academic: The fundamental, structural, and functional unit of all living organisms. It is the smallest unit of life that can replicate independently.

examples: Red blood cells carry oxygen in your body.
Nerve cells send messages to your brain.
An amoeba is a single-celled organism.

common_misconceptions: All cells look the same. (False: Cells have radically different shapes depending on their function. A nerve cell looks like a long wire, while a skin cell looks like a flat tile).
ai_context.tutor_hint: Remember Robert Hooke! He discovered cells in 1665 by looking at a piece of cork under a microscope. He called them 'cells' because they looked like little rooms.
